transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… I guess I came in because things at home have been a lot lately. My sister and her baby moved back in, and ever since then I’ve just been more on edge, kind of down, snapping at dumb little stuff around the house.

And then I’ll go to class or to the shop already feeling wiped out, which is annoying because I’m still doing okay, like I’m not completely falling apart. But I’ve missed a couple deadlines, and I backed out of helping with the theater set because I just couldn’t keep all the stuff straight in my head.
Have you been feeling anxious or worried about things lately?

Yeah, I guess anxious is fair. Like, I don’t know if I’m worried about one specific thing all the time, but since my sister and her baby moved back in, I’m just… more on edge. Stuff at the house gets to me way faster, and then I’m already drained when I get to class or the shop.

It’s weird because I’m still mostly getting by, but I’ve missed a couple deadlines, and I backed out of helping with the theater set because I couldn’t keep everything straight in my head.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the day?

Not most of the day, I don’t think. It’s more like… since my sister and the baby moved back in, I’ve been down more than usual, but it comes mixed with being on edge too. Like I’ll snap over some tiny thing at home, and then I’m already drained by the time I get to class or the shop.

I’m still getting by, mostly, but I’ve missed a couple deadlines, and I even backed out of helping with the theater set because I just couldn’t keep everything straight.
Have you been enjoying things you normally like to do?

I mean… I’m not totally sure. I haven’t really thought about it that way. I still like the stuff I like, I guess, but lately I’ll start doing something and then get distracted by everything else going on.

Like with the theater set thing, I used to like being around that kind of project, but then it started feeling like one more thing on the pile. But I don’t know if that’s “not enjoying it” or just… having too much happening, you know?
Have you noticed any change in your weight recently?

Uh… I don’t think so? I haven’t really been checking, honestly. My jeans feel about the same, I guess. I mean, with work clothes it’s hard to tell because half the time they’re already kind of loose or gross from the shop, but… no, nothing I’ve noticed.
Do you often worry about what might happen in the future?

I don’t know… I mean, I think everybody worries about the future, right? Like with school and work and whether I’m going to end up stuck doing the same thing forever. My uncle actually did that—he was at this one plant for, I think, like twenty-something years, and he always said the machines changed more than the people did, which is kind of funny but also not.

But, uh… if you mean like do I sit around constantly worrying about what’s going to happen, I’m not sure. I haven’t really been tracking it that way.
Do you find yourself worrying about things even when there's no obvious reason to worry?

I’m not really sure. Sometimes I’ll get kind of caught up thinking about stuff, but whether there’s “no reason” or not… I don’t know, there’s usually some reason if I think about it long enough.

Like even at the shop, if a machine makes a weird noise, everyone’s like, “that’s probably nothing,” but then you start thinking about how one little part can mess up the whole thing. Sorry, that’s probably not what you meant. I guess I haven’t noticed myself worrying out of nowhere, exactly.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things for more than a few days at a time?

More than a few days… I don’t know. Maybe? It depends what counts, I guess. Like if something’s hanging over me, I’ll think about it on and off, but I don’t know if I’d call it worrying the whole time.

Sometimes it’s just in the background, like when you leave a tool somewhere and you’re trying to remember where, and then you get distracted because somebody needs help with a lift or something. So… I haven’t really kept track of it like that.
Do you find yourself worrying about things almost every day?

Almost every day? I’m not sure… I don’t really count it like that. Some days I’ll think about stuff a lot, and other days I’m just busy and it doesn’t really register.

It’s kind of like when you’ve got a machine running and there’s this hum in the background—you don’t notice it until somebody points it out, and then you’re like, was that happening the whole time? So… I don’t know if I’d say almost every day. I haven’t really paid attention that closely.
Do you find yourself worrying about things even when there are no problems happening in your life?

I don’t really know. I mean, if there’s literally nothing going on, I don’t think I sit around worrying just to worry.

But then again, there’s always something, right? Like bills, work stuff, whether I forgot to tighten something down at the shop—though that’s probably more just normal thinking. Sometimes my brain kind of keeps checking things, like when you shut off a machine and still hear it in your head for a while. But I don’t know if that counts as worrying when there aren’t problems. I haven’t really noticed it that way.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things even when everything in your life seems to be going well?

I’m not really sure. If everything’s going well, I don’t think I’m sitting there thinking, “Oh no, what’s next?” or anything like that.

But it’s hard to say what “going well” means, you know? Like at work, even if the day’s fine, there’s always some little thing—someone borrowed a wrench and didn’t put it back, or a machine’s making a noise that might be nothing. I’ll think about that kind of stuff, but I don’t know if that’s worry or just… paying attention.

So, I guess I haven’t really noticed worrying when things are actually okay.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things for no specific reason?

For no specific reason… I don’t know. I guess I haven’t really caught myself doing that.

Usually if I’m thinking about something, there’s some hook to it, even if it’s small. Like if a tool went missing at work, I’ll be thinking about where it ended up, and then that reminds me of this one guy who always puts stuff back in the wrong drawer—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

So, yeah… I’m not sure I worry for no reason. I haven’t noticed it like that.
Do you often feel like you're worrying about something, even when you're not thinking about anything in particular?

I don’t think so… or at least I haven’t noticed it that way. Like, usually if I feel worked up, there’s some thought attached to it, even if it’s a dumb little thing.

But “not thinking about anything in particular” is kind of hard, because my mind is always sort of bouncing around. Like I’ll be at work and not thinking about one specific problem, but then I’m noticing the sound of the equipment, or whether something got put back right, or whatever. That’s probably not what you mean.

So… no, I guess I can’t really say I often feel worried with nothing in my head.
Do you often feel like you are worrying about things in general, even when there is not something specific bothering you?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way. Like “things in general” sounds kind of like just a cloud hanging over everything, and I don’t know if that’s really me.

I mean, I’ll get stuck thinking about stuff, but usually it’s tied to something—even if it’s just small. Like if something’s off at work, or I’m trying to remember if I put something back where it goes. Actually, the other day I spent way too long looking for this one socket because I was sure I’d set it on the bench, and then it was in my pocket the whole time… but that’s probably not what you’re asking.

So, no, I don’t think I’m worrying about everything in general when nothing specific is bothering me. Or at least I haven’t noticed that.
Do you think your worry is greater than what most people would experience in your situation?

Maybe… yeah, I think it might be more than most people would have, but I don’t know how to measure that.

I came in because since my sister and her baby moved back home, I’ve just been more on edge and kind of down than I usually am. Like little stuff around the house sets me off, and then I’ll get to class or the shop already worn out, before anything even happens there.

I’m still doing what I have to, mostly. It’s not like everything fell apart. But I’ve missed a couple deadlines, and I backed out of helping with the theater set because I just couldn’t keep everything straight. Which is annoying, because I actually like that kind of work—measuring, cutting, making stuff fit. But lately it feels like my head’s already full before the day starts.
Do you feel like you've been worrying almost every day since your sister and her baby moved back in?

Yeah… I mean, pretty much since they moved back in, so about a month now.

Not every single minute or anything, but most days it’s been there in some form. It’s weird because a month doesn’t sound that long when I say it, but it kind of feels like the house rhythm changed overnight, like where stuff goes and when it’s quiet and all that. But yeah—the worrying, or being keyed up about it, has been going on about a month.
Do you feel like you've been worrying about something almost every day since your sister and her baby moved back in?

Yeah, I’d say so. Since my sister and the baby moved back in, it’s been almost every day in some way.

It’s been about a month now, I think. I keep thinking it should feel normal by now, like when you rearrange a toolbox and after a week you stop reaching for the old drawer, but it hasn’t really clicked like that. So yeah… about a month of it being on my mind most days.
Do you feel like you're worrying about something almost every day, even when there aren't any obvious problems?

I’m not totally sure. Like, I notice it more when something’s actually happening at home, or I’m expecting things to be noisy or hectic, you know? 

If there’s nothing obvious going on, I don’t know… sometimes I still feel like I’m waiting for something to come up, but I couldn’t say it’s every day for no reason. I kind of have to think about it. It’s like when a machine’s been making a weird sound and then even when it stops, you’re still listening for it. But I don’t know if that counts as worrying.
Do you feel like you're worrying about something almost every day, regardless of what's happening?

I don’t know if I can say regardless of what’s happening. Like, I get what you mean, but it’s hard to separate it out.

Some days it’s tied to stuff going on at home, and then other times I’m just sort of… braced for it, I guess. But I don’t want to say it’s every day no matter what, because I haven’t really kept track. I’m not great at tracking stuff unless it’s like hours on a job sheet or parts inventory, you know? Then I can tell you exactly what’s missing. With this, it’s more fuzzy.
Do you think your worry about your sister and her baby living with you is worse than what most people would feel in your situation?

I don’t know if it’s worse than what most people would feel. I mean, anybody would be stressed with a baby in the house and everything changing, right? But it does feel like it’s getting to me more than I expected.

I came in because since my sister and the baby moved back, I’ve been more on edge and kind of down than usual. Like I’ll snap over dumb little stuff at home, and then I get to class or the shop already tired, like I used up all my patience before the day even started. I’m still getting by, it’s not like everything fell apart, but I’ve missed a couple deadlines and I backed out of helping with the theater set because I just couldn’t keep all the pieces straight. So… maybe it is more than normal, I guess.

I don’t know if it’s worse than what most people would feel. I mean, anybody would be stressed with a baby in the house and everything changing, right? But it does feel like it’s getting to me more than I expected.

I came in because since my sister and the baby moved back, I’ve been more on edge and kind of down than usual. Like I’ll snap over dumb little stuff at home, and then I get to class or the shop already tired, like I used up all my patience before the day even started. I’m still getting by, it’s not like everything fell apart, but I’ve missed a couple deadlines and I backed out of helping with the theater set because I just couldn’t keep all the pieces straight. So… maybe it is more than normal, I guess.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with symptoms of depressed mood, irritability, and fatigue, which have been persistent since their sister and her baby moved back in, indicating a depressive episode.
